[PREFERENCE] User is interested in audiobooks similar to "Sapiens."  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended audiobooks include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "Guns, Germs, and Steel" by Jared Diamond: Explores how geography, technology, and biology shaped human history.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "The Sixth Extinction: An Unnatural History" by Elizabeth Kolbert: Delves into the current mass extinction event caused by human activity.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "A Short History of Nearly Everything" by Bill Bryson: Provides an overview of sciences from the Big Bang to civilization.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "The Selfish Gene" by Richard Dawkins: Explores evolution through genetics.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "The Uninhabitable Earth: Life After Warming" by David Wallace-Wells: Examines the consequences of climate change.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "The Emperor of All Maladies: A Biography of Cancer" by Siddhartha Mukherjee: Discusses the history of cancer research and treatment.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "The Ancestors' Tale: A Pilgrimage to the Dawn of Evolution" by Richard Dawkins: Explores the history of life on Earth.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "The Ends of the World: Volcanic Apocalypses, Lethal Oceans, and Our Quest to Understand Earth's Past Mass Extinctions" by Peter Brannen: Discusses Earth's history of mass extinctions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "The Meaning of Human Existence" by Edward O. Wilson: Explores the significance of human existence.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "Origins: How the Earth Made Us" by Lewis Dartnell: Examines geological and astronomical factors shaping human history.  
[PREFERENCE] User is particularly interested in "The Sixth Extinction" and "The Emperor of All Maladies."  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "The Sixth Extinction" narrated by Anne Twomey: Engaging, clear, and well-paced with a neutral American accent.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "The Emperor of All Maladies" narrated by Stephen Hoye: Clear, concise, and measured with a neutral American accent.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Both narrators enhance the listening experience and convey the authors' voices effectively.
